newsitem.title: USA: Calif construction volume totals $2.65 bln in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Calif construction volume totals $2.65 bln in Sept.

text.p: California construction volume for September totalled $2.65 billion, according to a Construction Industry Research Board report Thursday.
Seasonally adjusted, the September total, which measures permits and contract awards, was down 3.7 percent from August, but up 8.9 percent from September 1995.
The Research Board said it was now forcasting total construction in 1996 of $31.83 billion, up 5.7 percent from 1995 and the highest construction volume total since 1991.
Construction volume should reach $36.05 billion in 1997, up 12.9 percent from 1996, and $38.26 billion in 1998, the Research Board said in a statement.

"We are seeing a steady response to job growth," said Ben Bartolotto, Research Board director. "We expect a progression of growth over the next two years in heavy construction due to increased funding for seismic retrofit work."
The Research Board said it based its forecasts on anticipated gains in residential and nonresidential building.
